newsitem.title: USA: Stocks extend rally on fresh signs of mild inflation.
newsitem.headline: Stocks extend rally on fresh signs of mild inflation.

text.p: Stocks jumped again Friday on more signs of steady economic growth with mild inflation, extending a week-long rally that has sent the Dow Jones industrial average up nearly 500 points.

Just after 1:15 p.m. EDT, the blue-chip index was up 74.64 points at 7,786.11. In the broader market, advances outpaced gainers by a 2-1 margin on volume of 316 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow finished at 7,305.29 on June 5 before the latest surge began in earnest. If the Dow ends with a gain Friday it would be the sixth straight record for the index of 30 blue chips.
The Nasdaq composite index rose about 13.09 to 1,424.41 as bellwether Intel Corp. rebounded, along with several other key technology stocks.

Stocks rose as the bond market rallied on news of a 0.3 percent decline in the May Producer Price Index -- the fifth consecutive monthly drop. The evidence that inflation remained in check reduced chances of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates in July.
The benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury rose 21/32, or $6.56 on a $1,000 bond, reducing its yield to 6.72 percent from 6.77 percent at Thursday's close.
"These inflation numbers have been extraordinary and totally unexpected by Wall Street," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood.
"The market is in some ways feeding on itself," said William Raftery, a technical analyst at Smith Barney. "A good market does beget a good market."
Analysts said this week's rally also came as money managers started making portfolio adjustments for the upcoming end of the second quarter.
"Most of the people who have been bearish are just throwing in the towel," said Charles Payne, head analyst at Wall Street Strategies. "I just think it is more of what we've been seeing," he said.
Brown said a recent increase of foreign participation in the rally, which he attributed to political instability in Europe, was another key factor.
Blue-chip stocks have been thriving all week, with drug shares, timber and household issues showing particular strength.
DuPont Co. rose 2-3/4 to 60-5/8 after being upgraded to a strong buy from outperform by Morgan Stanley. Merck & Co. Inc. gained 1-1/4 to 98-3/4 and Johnson & Johnson was up one to to 66-1/2.
Philip Morris Cos Inc. climbed 1-1/2 to 46-1/8 and was the most actively traded stock on the New York Stock Exchange while RJR Nabisco Holdings gained 3/4 to 34-7/8.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks climbed 9.73 to 893.21. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.01 to 629.13.
